title: How many checkerboard photos does OpenCV camera calibration need before the focal length stops moving?
lede: on OpenCV's 13 real checkerboard photos, random subsets of 3 views put the focal length within 2% of the 13-view value in 99% of draws (5–95% band 2.3% wide), 12 views give 0.5%; noise-only re-renders predict the band, and a one-term lens model doubles held-out error. One camera, one board
summary: Calibrates a camera with cv2.calibrateCamera on random subsets of the 13 real 640×480 checkerboard photos shipped with OpenCV (Apache-2.0), against the same model's all-view fit. With the default five-term model the 5–95% band of the focal length is 2.3% wide at 3 views and 0.49% at 12, and 99–100% of draws are within ±2%. Re-rendering the same board poses with Gaussian noise at the measured 0.41 px reprojection error and a known truth gives 3.0% and 0.8%, so sampling noise alone predicts the spread. A lean model (one radial term, centred principal point) has a 4.4% band on real photos against 2.0% on matching synthetic ones, and 0.43 px held-out reprojection error against 0.21 px for the full model at 12 views. Limits: one camera, one tutorial board with strongly tilted views; the reference is the all-view fit, not a lens ground truth; the 12-view row overlaps heavily (13 distinct subsets); synthetic noise is isotropic Gaussian.
